best_for: Programmers who want a fast, light editor with build commands and plugins on an older laptop or a Linux desktop, without the weight of a full IDE.

points.title: Light, with IDE touches
points.text: Geany sits between a plain text editor and a full IDE. It starts quickly and still gives you syntax support for more than 50 programming languages.

points.title: Plugins fill the gaps
points.text: Six plugins come with Geany, including a file browser and split window. The separate Geany-Plugins set adds Git and SVN support, spell checking and project tools.

points.title: Plugins ship differently per OS
points.text: The macOS disk image includes Geany-Plugins. On Windows the plugins are a separate installer you download on top.

points.title: Free under the GPL
points.text: Geany is GPL v2 open source with no paid edition and no account.

points.title: Windows is 64-bit and machine-wide
points.text: The Windows installer is 64-bit only and installs for all users, so it needs administrator rights. The Windows listing keeps 4 versions.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is not verified
points.text: Flathub does not mark the Geany Flatpak as verified, though it is published under the Geany Team name. Most Linux users can also install Geany from their distribution. macOS and Linux list only the current release here.
